content: 1. Topiramate was evaluated for its efficacy in treating chronic low back pain in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study conducted in 2006. The study included adults with a mean age of 42–49 years and was conducted in high-income countries. The maximum dosage of topiramate administered was 300 mg/day. 2. Gabapentin was assessed for its ability to reduce chronic benign nociceptive pain in a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study conducted in 2000. The dosage was individualized at 15 mg/kg, rounded to the nearest 300 mg. The study only reported group-level data, which was analyzed similarly to parallel studies. 3. Imprecision was noted in the pooled estimate, which crossed the null and the threshold for a small effect. This led to a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 4. Two parallel trials (Muehlbacher 2006, McCleane 2001) and one crossover trial (McCleane 2000) were conducted in high-income countries, involving adults with chronic low back pain (mean ages 42–49 years). Gabapentin was used in one trial at a dosage of up to 1200 mg/day and in another trial with an individualized dosage of 15 mg/kg, rounded to the nearest 300 mg. The crossover trial reported only group-level data, analyzed in the same manner as parallel studies. 5. Inconsistency was observed, with an I² value greater than 50%, which was not explained by stratified or sensitivity analyses. This resulted in a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 6. A parallel trial (Muehlbacher 2006) conducted in Germany included adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 49 years). Topiramate was administered at a maximum dosage of 300 mg/day. 7. Inconsistency could not be assessed due to the presence of only one study, leading to a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 8. Imprecision was significant due to the absence of a pooled estimate and fewer than 100 participants in the study, resulting in a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 9. A crossover trial (McCleane 2000) conducted in Ireland included adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 42 years). Gabapentin was administered with an individualized dosage of 15 mg/kg, rounded to the nearest 300 mg. The trial reported only group-level data, analyzed similarly to parallel studies. 10. One parallel trial (McCleane 2001) and one crossover trial (McCleane 2000) were conducted in Ireland, involving adults with chronic low back pain (mean ages 42–44 years). Gabapentin was used at a dosage of up to 1200 mg/day in one trial and an individualized dosage of 15 mg/kg, rounded to the nearest 300 mg, in the other. The crossover trial reported only group-level data, analyzed in the same manner as parallel studies. 11. Imprecision was noted in the pooled estimate, which crossed the null and the threshold for a large effect. This led to a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 12. A parallel trial (McCleane 2001) conducted in Ireland included adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 44 years). Gabapentin was administered at a dosage of up to 1200 mg/day. 13. A parallel randomized trial (Foster 2001) conducted in the USA included adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 47 years). Botulinum toxin A was delivered via a single administration into the paravertebral muscles. 14. Inconsistency could not be assessed due to the presence of only one study, leading to a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 15. Imprecision was significant due to the absence of a pooled estimate and fewer than 100 participants in the study, resulting in a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 16. A crossover randomized trial (Cogné 2017) conducted in France included adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 38 years). Botulinum toxin A was delivered via a single administration into the paravertebral muscles. The crossover trial was analyzed similarly to a parallel trial. 17. Three parallel randomized trials (Foster 2001, Jazayeri 2011, Machado 2016) were conducted in high-income countries (USA) and Iran, involving adults with chronic low back pain (mean ages 42–50 years). Botulinum toxin A was delivered via a single administration into the paravertebral muscles. 18. Three parallel randomized trials (Foster 2001, Jazayeri 2011, Machado 2016) and one crossover trial (Cogné 2017) were conducted in high-income countries (USA, France) and Iran, involving adults with chronic low back pain (mean ages 38–50 years). Botulinum toxin A was delivered via a single administration into the paravertebral muscles. The crossover trial was analyzed similarly to a parallel trial. 19. Imprecision was noted in the pooled estimate, which crossed the null and the threshold for a large effect. This led to a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 20. Imprecision was noted due to fewer than 200 participants in the analysis, resulting in a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 21. A parallel randomized trial (Zaringhalam 2010) conducted in Iran included male adults with chronic low back pain (mean age 55 years). Baclofen was administered at 30 mg/day for five weeks and compared to no treatment. 22. Risk of bias was significant due to the lack of blinding of participants and caregivers, leading to a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 23. Inconsistency could not be assessed due to the presence of only one study, leading to a downgrade of one level in the certainty of evidence. 24. Imprecision was significant due to the absence of a pooled estimate and fewer than 100 participants in the study, resulting in a downgrade of two levels in the certainty of evidence. 25. Cannabinoids were evaluated for their effects on chronic low back pain in both short-term (<4 weeks) and long-term (≥4 weeks) treatments. Various modalities of administration, including smoking and ingestion, were used. However, no trials were available for synthesis in the WHO guideline on non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults.
